correctness.rationale: Set q=h+1, c=hm-1, u=floor(c/q); for residue r, admissible two-coin base costs from x-y congruent r mod m have least candidates A=r(m+1), B=(m-r)c, each repeated at +qm. Other congruence branches start after these first-two candidates by m(m+1)>qm or mc>qm, so the second threshold is min(max(A,B),min(A,B)+qm). Comparing c-qu against 0 determines the four pieces, maximizing w_r minus m yields g1=(m+1)u+(h-1)m-1+[q|m], and summing (w_r-r)/m gives the claimed genus. I independently implemented a three-denomination representation-count DP for every 3<=m<=24 and 2<=h<m (253 parameter pairs), checked all second thresholds, g1 and n1 exactly; no exception. All-unrestricted quantifiers rest on the symbolic branch inequalities, not the finite check.
